source_locator.description: The next morning some young men gossip in front of a shop while Gunasekaran brushes his teeth nearby.

translation.english_text: (The next morning, some young men stand gossiping in front of a shop. Near them, Gunasekaran is brushing his teeth. Then—)
notes: The source uses `மைனர்கள்`; the English stage direction uses `young men` to avoid the misleading modern age/legal sense of `minors`, while exact dialogue labels remain unchanged.

translation.english_text: Where were you, man? Didn't see you all night.
Cards all night—my eyes are burning!
So your eyes burned! Did you at least get any money? Mm... that's exactly what you didn't.
Where's Venu? Can't see him anywhere.
The man's gone to lie on a soft bed. You know that idli seller Kalyani! Our fellow wagged his tail at her... his scheme didn't work... poor fellow got a good beating.
notes: `வால் ஆட்டியிருக்கான்` is retained as the animal-image `wagged his tail`; `பாச்சா பலிக்கலே` is rendered conservatively as his scheme not working rather than assigned a more specific game or trick.

translation.english_text: Hey, keep quiet! Why are you flapping your mouth for nothing too? Some fellow wandering around in a madman's disguise is also Kalyani's illicit lover...
notes: The colloquial `ஒட்டையை வீணு அலட்டிக்கிட்டே?` is rendered as idle mouth-flapping/chatter; the Tamil is not normalized.
`கள்ளப்புருஷன்` is translated explicitly as `illicit lover`, preserving the defamatory force that triggers Gunasekaran's reaction.

source_locator.description: Gunasekaran hears the slander and becomes angry.

translation.english_text: (Beating the young men.) What did you say—a stain on my Kalyani? Kalyani is my sister, my sister! I'm going right now to tell her who I am.
notes: The beating action is embedded inside the immutable dialogue record; it therefore remains inside this translation unit.
`களங்கம்` is retained as the source's stain/disgrace image rather than expanded into a more specific accusation.

source_locator.description: Gunasekaran runs furiously toward his sister's house.

translation.english_text: (He runs furiously toward his sister's house.)

source_locator.description: Gunasekaran does not find Kalyani in the hut.

translation.english_text: Circumstance made my sister a widow; society did not let her live. (Not finding Kalyani, he turns back. On the way...)
notes: The source's paired accusation `சந்தர்ப்பம்... சமுதாயம்...` is kept as `circumstance... society...`; the embedded return direction remains within the dialogue record.

translation.english_text: Sir, around here, a widow with a child...
Hey, is that a woman you know? Go look over there in that crowd. She committed suicide.
Ah—Kalyani! (He learns that the dead woman there is not Kalyani and returns.)

source_locator.description: Kalyani gives up her idli business in Madurai and leaves the town.

translation.english_text: [Kalyani gives up her idli business in Madurai and leaves the town altogether.]
